founding_note: The substrate shell is a reader-AND-controller UI (KIT_DIARY finding 18): it renders every substrate event AND causes them (create/rename/turn/interrupt/end/patch). Non-negotiable per Architect 2026-09-08. Total coverage — every visual state named, no shade uncovered.

shell_entities.name: Window

shell_entities.name: WindowStrip
shell_entities.definition: The top-of-window row above the first pane; carries the traffic-light dots. Blank per D46 — an entity because it shows/hides on single-pane vs multi-pane state.

shell_entities.name: Pane
shell_entities.definition: A leaf in a window's split tree; carries at most one Session; owns focus, dim, editing, drop-hint, split-tree position.

shell_entities.name: PaneHeader
shell_entities.definition: The identical full header per Pane — substrate wordmark + status dot + session name + driver chip + ⌥ workspace chip + records + studio + ⌃`.

shell_entities.name: DriverChip
shell_entities.definition: The clickable driver-name pill on a PaneHeader; opens the DriverDropdown.

shell_entities.name: DriverDropdown

shell_entities.name: WorkspaceChip
shell_entities.definition: The ⌥ workspace pill on a PaneHeader; opens the WorkspacePopover; reads workspace shape.

shell_entities.name: WorkspacePopover
shell_entities.definition: The read-only informational popover anchored under a WorkspaceChip; shows path + shape + branch; frozen at seq 1.

shell_entities.name: Prompt
shell_entities.definition: The input line at the bottom of a Pane; ↵ sends; `/` opens SlashRouter; carries caret color per focus (Layer 7 tonal rule).

shell_entities.name: SlashRouter
shell_entities.definition: The command menu that grows upward out of a Prompt when the user types `/`; renders one row per matching SlashCommand.

shell_entities.name: SlashCommand
shell_entities.definition: One entry in the slash inventory — /list, /run, /inspect, /diff, /context, /model, /studio, /export, /exit.

shell_entities.name: Transcript
shell_entities.definition: The message + tool-cycle event log rendered in a Pane's body (terminal level) or in the left column of the Reveal.

shell_entities.name: DelegateInline
shell_entities.definition: The `⑂` line in a Transcript representing one delegate call; folds to one line by default; click expands to child inset; `⏎` descends.

shell_entities.name: FanOutInline
shell_entities.definition: The `⑂ delegate → N children` line in a Transcript representing one delegate call with multiple children; expands to a child list; ↑↓/↵ walks; ↵ descends.

shell_entities.name: Descent
shell_entities.definition: The pane-focus stack from the session down into a delegate child. Depth 0 = session; 1–2 inside a child (engine cap per D41).

shell_entities.name: Reveal
shell_entities.definition: The revealed-machinery state of a Pane; renders transcript-left + machinery-right with a draggable gutter between them.

shell_entities.name: Lens
shell_entities.definition: A machinery view mode — one of stream+graph, i/o, structure, scene.

shell_entities.name: Stream
shell_entities.definition: The scrollable event-row list in the stream+graph Lens; each row shows seq · t · kind · producer · gist; clicking opens an Inspector.

shell_entities.name: SideGraph
shell_entities.definition: The pinned horizontal gantt (in `→` direction) or the inline down-lane cells (in `⇅` direction); one lane per producer kind; spans are call intervals.

shell_entities.name: Inspector
shell_entities.definition: The inline expansion under a Stream row showing schema · time · producer · content · payload; click same row again to close.

shell_entities.name: Surface
shell_entities.definition: A summoned full-window view — one of records, studio, assay; esc returns to the prior level.

shell_entities.name: Records
shell_entities.definition: The records Surface — workspace-grouped session and record list; assay click-through; click a session to switch pane.

shell_entities.name: Assay
shell_entities.definition: The assay board Surface — arms × cases × trials bars with verdict words, preregistration banner, underpowered banner.

shell_entities.name: Studio
shell_entities.definition: The studio Surface — form ⇄ canvas topology authoring at parity with substrate's TopologyBuilder; validate; build & launch.

shell_entities.name: Find
shell_entities.definition: The ⌘F search bar over a Pane's current focused lens; scope is transcript or stream; matches paint bright while rest dim to 0.35.

shell_entities.name: Settings
shell_entities.definition: The ⌘, modal — theme, type size, nested-descent, bindings.

shell_entities.name: ExportDialog
shell_entities.definition: The /export modal — pick .record dir or events.jsonl and target path.

shell_entities.name: EndConfirm
shell_entities.definition: The /exit confirm modal — end-session interrupts a live turn and finalises the record.

shell_entities.name: FirstRun
shell_entities.definition: The first-run driver picker — probes local Ollama, CLI drivers on PATH, API keys in env, deterministic floor; ↵ starts.

shell_entities.name: Footer
shell_entities.definition: The persistent one-line bottom bar — session-status swatch · record identity · esc/⌃` hint.

shell_entities.name: DropHint
shell_entities.definition: The zone-highlight overlay drawn on a Pane during a header-drag; one of five zones (W, E, N, S, C); previews the drop outcome.

shell_entities.name: Gutter
shell_entities.definition: A drag-resize handle between two Panes or between transcript and machinery; ⌥ modifier promotes to full-line drag.

shell_entities.name: Collection
shell_entities.definition: The whole-UI ephemeral state — windows × pane grids × pane→session bindings × per-pane level + lens + focus + collapsed states. Persisted for whole-state restore.

shell_entities.name: Anchor
shell_entities.definition: A deterministic pixel-anchor painted at a fixed known coordinate encoding one byte of shell state; the Playwright harness screenshots + PNG-decodes the anchor to reconstruct the state. Every load-bearing shell state has one.

substrate_reference_entities.name: Session
substrate_reference_entities.definition: A substrate session; the SessionManifest row in session_registry — session_id, name, driver, workspace, workspace_shape, bundle, seed, role, status, record_root, tools, driver_params.

substrate_reference_entities.name: Record
substrate_reference_entities.definition: The append-only event log for a Session; on disk at ~/.substrate/sessions/<sid>/record/events-*.jsonl; replayable byte-identically.

substrate_reference_entities.name: Envelope
substrate_reference_entities.definition: One event on a Record — {crc, kind, payload, producer, schema, seq, t}. `kind` is drawn from substrate.constants + substrate.topologies.session.vocabulary.

substrate_reference_entities.name: Producer
substrate_reference_entities.definition: A substrate producer instance emitting events; has kind (model/tool/park/session_end/…), instance id, parent.

substrate_reference_entities.name: Driver
substrate_reference_entities.definition: The Responder backing a Session — DeterministicResponder | CliResponder(claude|gemini) | OllamaResponder(<model>).

substrate_reference_entities.name: Workspace
substrate_reference_entities.definition: A directory bound to a Session; shape ∈ {flat, worktree, isolate}; frozen at seq 1 (SessionManifest.workspace + workspace_shape).

substrate_reference_entities.name: Bundle
substrate_reference_entities.definition: A context bundle attached to a Session (methodology / personality / per_turn / tools / role / parent_context); shipped defaults live at substrate.bundles.

substrate_reference_entities.name: Tools
substrate_reference_entities.definition: The per-session tool allowlist (SessionManifest.tools) — sorted list of tool names or None for unrestricted.

substrate_reference_entities.name: Turn
substrate_reference_entities.definition: One session turn — UserMessage → PromptComposed → ModelReply → (ToolCall × N + ToolResult × N)* → FinalAnswer → Park; turn_index is under-lock (session_registry.py:799).

substrate_reference_entities.name: DelegateCall
substrate_reference_entities.definition: A substrate ToolCall{tool:'delegate'} in a Turn; the ToolResult carries {answer, child_root, steps} and the child_root points at a child Record. Depth cap max_depth=2.

substrate_reference_entities.name: Trigger
substrate_reference_entities.definition: A named starter in a substrate topology; fires a Producer when its Predicate over a View matures. Emits `substrate.TriggerFired`. The Structure lens renders triggers; the Studio form authors them.

substrate_reference_entities.name: View
substrate_reference_entities.definition: A running projection of the Bus a Predicate reads (KindCount / KindBuffer / …). Referenced by Triggers. The Structure lens shows the view list; the Studio form authors them.

substrate_reference_entities.name: Route
substrate_reference_entities.definition: A staging rule that carries an event of a named kind into a future Producer's named input slot. The Studio form authors routes; the Studio canvas draws them as dashed edges into slot nodes.

substrate_reference_entities.name: TerminationPolicy
substrate_reference_entities.definition: The composed condition under which a Run finalises; six named policies (quiescence_with_watchdog, all_completed, threshold_count, cancel_all_others, any_of, all_of). The Structure lens renders the policy; the Studio chips select it.

surfaced_for_ratification.note: DelegateInline is the ⑂ line the shell renders; DelegateCall is the substrate ToolCall it renders FROM. Two entities, one bounded context each — the shell owns render state (folded/expanded, descend-focus), substrate owns wire state (child_root, depth, ok, error). Proposed disposition: KEEP AS TWO ENTITIES (DDD bounded contexts) — Layer 2 payloads reference DelegateCall via its child_root and depth; Layer 5 pairs them with an ordering invariant.

FanOutInline is one ⑂ line for a delegate call producing multiple children. Substrate models this as one DelegateCall whose ToolResult carries multiple child_roots. Proposed disposition: KEEP FanOutInline as a distinct shell entity (its expanded state and ↑↓/↵ walk are shell-only).
Not surfaced as a Layer 0 entity — a recursive tree over Panes, not a thing state is tracked ON. If FD-2 lands the split-tree layout, that changes; propose a Layer 0 entity SplitNode then.

The editor level and its modes (code / documents / images / video / plain-shell) are SPECULATIVE per DESIGN-SPEC §5. Not in v0.1 Layer 0. When they ratify, they land as new entities in a v0.2 bump via NEW_TAG/PAYLOAD_FIELD proposals.

Rendered by the OS via Electron, not by the shell renderer. Its state (which menu open, which item hovered) is machine-readable via Electron's `Menu` API, not through pixel-anchors. Proposed disposition: NOT in Layer 0 (OS-owned surface) — but the menu ITEMS map to existing shell tags (the menu items are alternative entry points to the same verbs). Surface at the appropriate sprint.

Rendered as a `◌ rate-limited · retry 3/6 in 14s` line inside a Transcript per 19i; substrate emits SessionWarning{kind:...}. Currently modeled as a Transcript row rendering, not as its own shell entity. Question: does `RateLimitedWaiting` earn its own Layer 0 entity? Proposed disposition: NO — it's a Transcript render of a substrate SessionWarning; the shell state is `is_rate_limited: bool` on the focused Session's derived status.

layer_1_lexical.note: Tag form: {ENTITY_SNAKE_UPPER}_{VERB_PAST_PARTICIPLE_UPPER}. Every tag is emitted at the reducer-commit that changes shell state; the emit lands as a JSONL line in the harness trace AND flips a pixel-anchor testid the harness reads (Architect 2026-09-08 non-negotiable). Category = architectural boundary (14 categories). Stratum = event | ambient | summary | incident (per Foundation 01, PRINCIPLES §Layer 6/7). Passive-render entities (WindowStrip, PaneHeader, DriverChip, WorkspaceChip, Footer, Records, Assay) produce zero shell-emit tags — they are paint witnesses of ancestor entities' state; Layer 7 (Evidence) will pair them with pixel-anchors. Substrate-owned entities do not get shell-emit tags — the shell renders substrate wire strings (RunStarted, UserMessage, Park, …); the reader-side integration lives in Layer 5 (State-Transition) pairing rules. The reader-AND-controller half — every shell-issued substrate call — appears here as `bridge` + `bridge_reply` categories.

layer_6_operators.note: Runtime / Operator layer per PRINCIPLES §Layer 6. Names how the program computed each event — the subsystems, their model routes, their fallback chains, their performance constraints. The shell runs across three process boundaries: renderer (Chromium in Electron), main (Node), bridge (Python). Every operator names which tags it EMITS and which tags it CONSUMES. Every LLM call lives inside a Responder inside substrate; the shell owns none. Substrate reference operators are named but not owned (grader-side read). Source-vs-observer convention (REVIEW-2026-09-10 Layer 6-10 O3/O4): where a tag traverses multiple operators (e.g. DriverResolver → DispatchLoop reply → BridgeClient → ShellReducer → Emitter → single JSONL line for PROBE_DRIVER_PROBED), the operator listed FIRST in the emits list is the source (the one that observes/generates the fact); subsequent operators are observers (they forward, they don't source). PROBE_DRIVER_PROBED/FAILED: source = DriverResolver, observer = BridgeClient. BRIDGE_DEAD_SURFACED: source = BridgeSupervisor, observer = BridgeClient.

operators.constraints: single-threaded; every state commit < 16ms; must not block on IPC (dispatch and continue; the reply lands asynchronously through BridgeClient)

operators.name: Emitter
operators.responsibilities: The single emit(kind, payload) call site (v0.1 emit.ts equivalent). Every ShellReducer commit that changes visible state passes through Emitter, which (1) validates against `signals/0.1.json` §layer_2_payload; (2) appends {t, kind, payload} to the in-memory buffer; (3) forwards to HarnessSink when `window.__substrateHarness` is truthy; (4) touches the paint anchor associated with the kind (Layer 7 pairing).
operators.emits: none directly — Emitter is the funnel, not a source
operators.consumes: every call from ShellReducer and RecordSubscriber
operators.constraints: throws on unknown kind (hard rule 2 — vocabulary is the contract); throws on payload validation failure (Draft-07 additionalProperties:false envelope-level)

operators.name: AnchorPainter
operators.responsibilities: The rAF loop that repaints Anchor testids from ShellState. Every load-bearing shell state carries a paint witness at a fixed data-testid; the harness reads pixels from a screenshot and decodes bytes back to state via Addendum A2. Non-negotiable per Architect 2026-09-08.
operators.consumes: ShellState via React subscription; rAF ticks
operators.constraints: rAF-gated (~60Hz); HARNESS_HEARTBEAT only fires when `window.__substrateHarness` is truthy (production builds pay zero rAF cost); every paint witness must be visible (B4 — never `visibility:hidden`)

operators.name: RecordSubscriber
operators.responsibilities: For each pane's bound session, tails `${record_root}/events-*.jsonl` via a bridge poll or SSE (implementation lands at Sprint 016); parses the envelope; forwards to ShellReducer which emits TRANSCRIPT_* tags matched to the envelope's kind + producer.
emits: TRANSCRIPT_ROW_RENDERED (× K, one per envelope arrival)
operators.note_review_2026_09_10_O2: TRANSCRIPT_AWAITING_FIRST_MESSAGE_RENDERED moved out of this operator (reader of record envelopes only) into ShellReducer, where it fires from bind at PANE_UNBOUND_BOUND before the first PROMPT_SUBMITTED. RecordSubscriber emits only from real record envelopes.
operators.constraints: event-cadence 1:1 with envelope arrivals (Layer 4 pairing); envelope order strictly by seq

operators.name: BridgeClient
operators.responsibilities: The renderer-side IPC channel exposed via `window.substrate.send({op, args})`. Correlates every *_REQUESTED with its reply by request_id (uuid4 hex 12-char minted at REQUESTED emit-site). Forwards replies back into ShellReducer which emits the matching *_ACKED or *_FAILED.
operators.consumes: bridge:message IPC events from BridgeSupervisor (via preload)
operators.constraints: one pending request per request_id at a time; timeouts per Layer 4 pairing bounds

operators.name: BridgeSupervisor
operators.responsibilities: Spawns the Python subprocess at app.whenReady; owns the child process handle; enforces the one-crash-then-banner policy (first crash → restart with 500ms backoff; second crash within 30s → pin the dead banner). Routes stdin/stdout as newline-delimited JSON; routes stderr to `<logs>/bridge.log`.
operators.emits: BRIDGE_DEAD_SURFACED (via IPC to renderer); process lifecycle events
operators.constraints: one Python subprocess per Electron app; ~30MB resident; SUBSTRATE_UI_PYTHON env var picks the interpreter (default python3)

operators.name: IPCRouter
operators.responsibilities: Wires `ipcMain.handle('bridge:send', …)` to the subprocess's stdin; forwards subprocess stdout lines to `mainWindow.webContents.send('bridge:message', msg)`. Buffers messages that arrive before the renderer's `did-finish-load` and flushes on ready.
operators.constraints: buffer flush at `did-finish-load`; no message dropped in the boot window (Layer 4 forbidden_after: no *_REQUESTED before BRIDGE_HELLO_RECEIVED)

operators.name: HarnessLogWriter
operators.responsibilities: When SUBSTRATE_HARNESS=1, opens an append stream to `<userData>/harness/last.jsonl`; every `harness:emit` IPC message writes one line. Overwritten at every launch (fresh trace per test run).
operators.constraints: best-effort — a write failure never breaks the reducer (preload try/catch guards)

operators.name: HarnessSink
operators.responsibilities: Preload exposes `window.__substrateHarness.append(sig)` when process.env.SUBSTRATE_HARNESS==='1'. Emitter calls it once per emit. Forwards via `ipcRenderer.send('harness:emit', sig)` to HarnessLogWriter.
operators.constraints: gated on env — production builds do not expose the sink to renderer JS

operators.name: HelloEmitter
operators.responsibilities: On Python subprocess start, imports substrate and emits `{op:hello, substrate:<version>, protocol:1}` to stdout. On import failure, emits `{op:halt, reason:substrate_import_failed, detail:<str>}` and exits 1.
operators.constraints: must produce hello within 3s of spawn (Layer 4 pairing)

operators.name: DispatchLoop
operators.responsibilities: Reads stdin line-by-line; parses JSON; routes to op handlers via OPS map. Long ops (submit_user_message) offloaded to a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) so the read loop stays free for interrupt.
operators.constraints: single-threaded stdin read; workers pool for long ops; every reply flushes

operators.name: RegistryProxy
operators.responsibilities: Builds substrate.session_registry.SessionRegistry with `session_topology_factory` injected at construction (else RuntimeError at first turn_sync — session_registry.py:779). Wraps every IPC op → registry method: list_all, get, create, set_name, set_driver, set_bundle, try_enqueue_turn/turn_sync/dequeue_turn, interrupt, delete.
operators.emits: none directly — DispatchLoop emits the wire replies
operators.constraints: session_registry uses per-session threading.Lock; turn_queue_cap=4 per session (session_registry.py:281); halts `bridge_mapping_required` at construction if factory is missing

operators.name: DriverResolver
operators.responsibilities: Resolves driver names to substrate.reference Responder instances. Three families: `deterministic` → DeterministicResponder (D69 floor; stateful; skips cache); `claude`/`gemini` → CliResponder (halts driver_unavailable:not_on_path if binary absent); any other → OllamaResponder probed via /api/show at construction (halts driver_unavailable:ollama:<name>:<ExcType> on probe failure).
operators.consumes: probe_driver op; every create_session and set_driver op

model_routes.ollama_any: substrate.reference.OllamaResponder(model=name, think=params.think or False, num_ctx=min(advertised, 262144), max_tokens=params.max_tokens or 0, timeout=params.timeout or 300.0)

operators.fallback_chain: PROBE_DRIVER_FAILED at create-time → the shell falls back to `deterministic` per D69 first-run rules; PROBE_DRIVER_FAILED on set_driver → keeps prior driver, surfaces failure to Header
operators.constraints: RESPONDER_CACHE keyed by (name, params) — DeterministicResponder skipped (stateful); every non-deterministic Responder outlives turns for the same params combo; `think=False` default (Ollama returns HTTP 400 for non-reasoning models; reasoning families opt-in via driver_params)

operators.name: ManifestWatcher
operators.responsibilities: Uses `watchfiles` (or Node fs.watch on the renderer side — implementation choice at Sprint 016) to monitor `~/.substrate/sessions/<sid>/manifest.json` for every bound session. Forwards status transitions (running/parked/interrupted/ended) to the renderer so PaneHeader status dots repaint.
operators.emits: status-change events into the bridge_reply channel (feeds Anchor repaints)
operators.consumes: filesystem writes from the SessionRegistry's per-session lock
operators.constraints: one watcher per bound session; teardown on PANE_CLOSED for that pane's session_id (unless another pane also binds the same session)

operators.name: SessionRegistry (substrate reference)
operators.responsibilities: Substrate's in-core SessionManifest store — JSON at `~/.substrate/sessions/<sid>/manifest.json` + index `by-name.json` under fcntl.flock; per-session threading.Lock; turn queue via try_enqueue_turn/dequeue_turn (cap=4). All shell writes go through here via RegistryProxy.
operators.emits: none (shell-side); substrate wire envelopes come from within turn_sync's Runtime
operators.cite: session_registry.py:96-149 SessionManifest, :400 create, :472 set_name, :645 set_bundle, :693 set_driver, :747 turn_sync, :912 interrupt, :993 delete

operators.name: SessionTopology (substrate reference)
operators.responsibilities: The substrate topology factory the bridge's RegistryProxy injects at SessionRegistry construction. Called per-turn as `(manifest, first_turn_user_message) -> topology`. Emits SessionStarted, UserMessage, PromptFragment × N, PromptComposed, ModelReply, ToolCall + ToolResult × M, FinalAnswer, Park, SessionEnded, TranscriptCompacted, SessionWarning.

operators.name: DelegateTool (substrate reference)
operators.responsibilities: The `delegate` tool in substrate.topologies.tool_loop. A parent session's model producer calls it; substrate spawns a child topology, records to `delegate_child_<hash>_c0`, folds back a ToolResult carrying {answer, child_root, steps}. max_depth=2 (delegate.py:353); refusal at depth 2 renders as failed ToolResult (SESSION_ENDED_MID_DELEGATE wire tag at :59 covers mid-turn child death).
operators.cite: topologies/tool_loop/delegate.py:353 max_depth, :436 depth-cap guard, :437-439 refusal raise (REVIEW-2026-09-10 Layer 6-10 line-number precision), :59 SESSION_ENDED_MID_DELEGATE

layer_7_evidence.note: Evidence layer per PRINCIPLES §Layer 7. Four kinds of constraint: (1) `tonal` — voice canon on user-facing strings; (2) `numeric_range` — bounds on integer/float fields; (3) `cross_reference` — foreign-key resolution; (4) `pixel_anchor` — the harness paint-witness testid a tag flips (Architect 2026-09-08 non-negotiable). Enforceability: `mechanical` (schema / regex / arithmetic), `llm_check` (prose / tone), `manual_review` (human). Every load-bearing state changes exactly one pixel-anchor byte; the harness reads it from a screenshot per Addendum A2. Passive-render entities pair with anchors even though they emit no tag — their paint witness is what the harness reads.

evidence_constraints.constraint: resolves to a live Layer 0 entity at emit time — pane_id ∈ ShellState.panes; session_id ∈ SessionManifest set (or minted for the pending SESSION_CREATE_REQUESTED); window_id ∈ open windows; tool_call_id from a real substrate ToolCall envelope; child_record_root exists on disk after DELEGATE_CALL_FOLDED; request_id matches exactly one bridge_request stratum instance
evidence_constraints.grader_check: at emit time, look up the id in the corresponding registry; grader post-processes the JSONL trace and flags any orphan id

evidence_constraints.constraint: the string is either a substrate kernel-lifecycle kind (substrate.constants:41-52 — twelve kinds), a substrate session-vocab kind (vocabulary.py:73-100 — ten kinds), or a downstream topology kind (ToolCall, ToolResult, FinalAnswer, or any application kind on the record). Open string per D26 full-granularity view.
evidence_constraints.enforceability: mechanical (grader reads bridge.log for the corresponding envelope on the same session_id + seq and matches the kind)

evidence_constraints.constraint: MUST equal empty string `""` — substrate deprecates the seed field per session_registry.py:421-431 (`SessionManifest.seed is deprecated. The prompt-composition arc moved every real prompt source to a PromptFragment producer; seed has no consumer inside the topology. Pass empty string; a future sprint drops the field`)

evidence_constraints.target: every user-facing string the shell generates (log/status lines, dialog notes, Studio output strings, error text)
evidence_constraints.constraint: lowercase leading words in log/status lines (Fowler-style); no emoji anywhere in strings the shell generates (D45; the tone canon in WORKING_AGREEMENT); labels never wrap (shrink → ellipsize → tooltip per D32); no narration prose (D40 — hints in tooltips, never on-screen body copy); no cost/money display anywhere (D45/D46)
evidence_constraints.enforceability: mechanical + llm_check — mechanical grep for emoji (Unicode ranges U+1F300–U+1FAFF, U+2600–U+26FF, U+2700–U+27BF) and for `$`/`¢`/`€`/`£` in shell-generated strings; llm_check for prose tone

evidence_constraints.target: no cost or money display anywhere in the shell
evidence_constraints.constraint: The shell renders zero dollar amounts, no per-call cost, no aggregate spend, no token-price conversion, no `$`/`¢`/`€`/`£` in any user-facing string, no ambient token counter converted to money. Context pressure (tokens_estimated vs driver_context_tokens) is the only token-adjacent surface (WINDOW-STRIP-EXPLORATION §2), and it renders as a fraction, never as currency.
evidence_constraints.enforceability: mechanical (grep for currency glyphs + regex for `\$\d`)

evidence_constraints.constraint: Every UI label shrinks → ellipsizes → tooltip per D32; prose wraps normally. Header labels (name, driver ▾, ⌥ workspace, records, studio, ⌃`) are labels; transcript rows are prose.
evidence_constraints.enforceability: manual_review + Playwright DOM assertion (`white-space: nowrap` on every `.label` class element)

evidence_constraints.constraint: The Emitter strips any key at any depth whose name matches `/key|token|secret|password/i` (case-insensitive) — replaces the value with the string `"[redacted]"` before write. Ollama's four documented params (think, max_tokens, num_ctx, timeout) never match; API-key-carrying param names always match. Runtime discipline, not schema-enforced.
evidence_constraints.enforceability: mechanical (test at emit-site: pass a `{claude_api_key: "sk-...", think: true}` object and grep the JSONL — the key value must not appear)

evidence_constraints.constraint: Draft-07 `oneOf` per key value: `theme` → both are enum `[dark|light|system]`; `type_size` → both are integer 9..19; `nested_descent` → both are boolean; `bindings` → both are objects of key-combo strings.
evidence_constraints.enforceability: mechanical (Draft-07 `oneOf` schema — the SETTING_CHANGED payload schema in Layer 2 has a `layer_7_constraint` field naming this; the concrete oneOf lands here)
evidence_constraints.schema_addendum: SETTING_CHANGED.payload = {type:object, additionalProperties:false, required:[key,from,to], oneOf:[ {properties:{key:{const:theme}, from:{enum:[dark,light,system]}, to:{enum:[dark,light,system]}}}, {properties:{key:{const:type_size}, from:{type:integer, minimum:9, maximum:19}, to:{type:integer, minimum:9, maximum:19}}}, {properties:{key:{const:nested_descent}, from:{type:boolean}, to:{type:boolean}}}, {properties:{key:{const:bindings}, from:{type:object}, to:{type:object}}} ]}
evidence_constraints.cite: REVIEW-2026-09-10 Layer 2/3 seed deprecation note + P2 flag

evidence_constraints.constraint: DELEGATE_CALL_RENDERED.depth ∈ [1,2]; DESCENT_ENTERED.depth ∈ [1,2]; DESCENT_EXITED.to_depth ∈ [0,1]; DELEGATE_DEPTH_CAP_REFUSED.depth = 2 (const). Substrate max_depth=2 at delegate.py:353.

At any moment, at most `turn_queue_cap` (default 4 per session_registry.py:281) turns can be enqueued for the same session_id. A fifth TURN_SUBMIT_REQUESTED for a session already at cap must produce TURN_SUBMIT_FAILED{reason: queue_full}. Grader counts pending turns per session across the JSONL trace.
Every window carries at most 8 panes (4 cols × 2 rows per D35). PANE_SPLIT that would create a 9th pane must not fire.
evidence_constraints.enforceability: mechanical (grader counts alive panes per window_id from PANE_CREATED − PANE_CLOSED)

evidence_constraints.target: every incident-stratum tag carries a diagnostic-required Evidence
evidence_constraints.constraint: STUDIO_VALIDATE_FAILED.errors + STUDIO_BUILD_REJECTED.errors (both required, minItems 1); SESSION_CREATE_FAILED.reason (required); SESSION_RENAME_FAILED.reason (required); TURN_SUBMIT_FAILED.reason (required, enumerated); DRIVER_CHANGE_FAILED.reason (required); BUNDLE_ATTACH_FAILED.reason (required); PROBE_DRIVER_FAILED.reason (required); BRIDGE_DEAD_SURFACED.crash_count (required, minimum 2); DELEGATE_DEPTH_CAP_REFUSED.depth (required, const 2). Every incident has a payload field that names the failure precisely enough to grade.
evidence_constraints.enforceability: mechanical (schema-enforced — every incident payload in Layer 2 carries the required reason/detail field)

evidence_constraints.target: every load-bearing shell state has a paint-witness testid the harness decodes
evidence_constraints.constraint: The AnchorPainter maintains the following testids. Each carries a single byte (grayscale rgb=b,b,b) at (0,0)-of-canvas. The harness screenshots the DOM, decodes each canvas per Addendum A2, reconstructs shell state, cross-validates against the JSONL trace + the bridge.log. If the three channels disagree the sprint fails.

rAF frame counter mod 256; only paints when window.__substrateHarness is truthy
